Description: The Royal Air Force is created by merging the Royal Flying Corps and the Royal Naval Air Service.
Event title: Creation of the Royal Air Force

Description: Generalísimo Francisco Franco announces the end of the Spanish Civil War after the last Republican forces surrender.
Event title: End of the Spanish Civil War

Description: An 8.6 magnitude earthquake in the Aleutian Islands generates a destructive tsunami that reaches Hawaii and causes dozens of deaths, mostly in Hilo.
The TIROS-1 satellite transmits the first television picture from space.
Iran becomes an Islamic republic by a 99% vote, officially overthrowing the Shah.
Same-sex marriage becomes legal in the Netherlands, the first contemporary country to allow it.
Event title: Legalization of Same-Sex Marriage in the Netherlands

Description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León comes ashore on what is now the U.S. state of Florida.
Event title: Ponce de León lands in Florida

Description: The Coinage Act is passed by Congress, establishing the United States Mint.
A British Royal Navy squadron defeats a smaller Dano-Norwegian Navy at the Battle of Copenhagen, forcing Denmark out of the Second League of Armed Neutrality.
Defeat at the Third Battle of Petersburg forces the Army of Northern Virginia and the Confederate government to abandon Richmond, Virginia.
President Wilson asks the U.S. Congress for a declaration of war on Germany.
Argentina invades the Falkland Islands, beginning the Falklands War.
The second of two treaties making up the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis is signed, ending the Italian Wars.
Robert Walpole becomes, in effect, the first Prime Minister of Great Britain, though he himself denied that title.
Union forces capture Richmond, Virginia, the capital of the Confederate States of America.
Gottlieb Daimler is granted a German patent for a light, high-speed, four-stroke engine, which he uses seven months later to create the world's first motorcycle, the Daimler Reitwagen.
U.S. President Harry S. Truman signs the Marshall Plan, authorizing $5 billion in aid for 16 countries.
Martin Cooper of Motorola makes the first handheld mobile phone call to Joel S. Engel of Bell Labs.
Francis Drake is knighted by Queen Elizabeth I for completing a circumnavigation of the world.
Napoleon abdicates conditionally for the first time and names his son Napoleon II as Emperor of the French.
Argonia, Kansas elects Susanna M. Salter as the first female mayor in the United States.
Twelve nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty creating the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated by James Earl Ray at a motel in Memphis, Tennessee.
People involved: Martin Luther King Jr.; James Earl Ray

Description: The MPLA government of Angola and UNITA rebels sign a peace treaty ending the Angolan Civil War.
Russian forces led by Alexander Nevsky rebuffed an invasion attempt by the Teutonic Knights during the Battle on the Ice of Lake Peipus.
United States President George Washington exercised his authority to veto a bill for the first time in United States history.
Chile's independence movement, led by Bernardo O'Higgins and José de San Martín, won a decisive victory over Spain, leaving 2,000 Spaniards and 1,000 Chilean patriots dead.
People involved: Bernardo O'Higgins; José de San Martín

Description: An F5 tornado in Tupelo, Mississippi, killed 233 people during the Tupelo–Gainesville tornado outbreak.
The Imperial Japanese Navy launched a carrier-based air attack on Colombo, damaging port and civilian facilities and sinking HMS Cornwall and HMS Dorsetshire southwest of Ceylon.
Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori dissolved the Peruvian congress by military force.
Mehmed II begins his siege of Constantinople, which falls on May 29 and is renamed Istanbul.
Jan van Riebeeck establishes a resupply camp at the Cape of Good Hope that eventually becomes Cape Town.
Event title: Dutch resupply camp established at the Cape

Description: Ships of the Continental Navy fail in their attempt to capture a Royal Navy dispatch boat.
The opening of the first modern Olympic Games is celebrated in Athens, 1,500 years after the original games were banned by Roman emperor Theodosius I.
During World War I, the United States declares war on Germany.
Event title: United States declares war on Germany

Description: Early Bird is launched as the first commercial communications satellite to be placed in geosynchronous orbit.
The first Corpus Juris Civilis, a fundamental work in jurisprudence, is issued by Eastern Roman Emperor Justinian I.
Empress Matilda becomes the first female ruler of England, adopting the title "Lady of the English".
Event title: Matilda becomes Lady of the English

Description: Bach's St John Passion, BWV 245, receives its premiere performance at St. Nicholas Church in Leipzig.
Event title: Premiere of Bach's St John Passion

Description: The Union's Army of the Tennessee and Army of the Ohio defeat the Confederate Army of Mississippi near Shiloh, Tennessee.
The World Health Organization is established by the United Nations.
Ayyubids of Egypt capture King Louis IX of France in the Battle of Fariskur.
Czar Alexander I officially announces the transfer of the status of the Finnish capital from Turku to Helsinki.
The Venus de Milo is discovered on the Aegean island of Milos.
Event title: Discovery of the Venus de Milo

Description: The French Third Republic and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland sign the Entente cordiale.
Historical entity: French Third Republic; United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

Description: A team of computer manufacturers, users, and university people led by Grace Hopper meets to discuss the creation of a new programming language that would be called COBOL.
A solar eclipse occurs, visible over areas of the Pacific Ocean and Latin American countries such as Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia and Venezuela.
Mongol forces defeated the Polish and German armies at the Battle of Liegnitz.
Robert Cavelier de La Salle discovered the mouth of the Mississippi River, claimed it for France, and named it Louisiana.
Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, effectively ending the American Civil War.
People involved: Robert E. Lee; Ulysses S. Grant

Description: Germany invaded Denmark and Norway during World War II in Operation Weserübung.
The Journey of Reconciliation, described as the first interracial Freedom Ride, began through the upper South in violation of Jim Crow laws.
During the Iraq War, Baghdad fell to American forces.
The settlement of Villa Imperial de Carlos V, now Potosí, is founded in Bolivia after the discovery of huge silver deposits.
The Statute of Anne, the first law regulating copyright, comes into force in Great Britain.
Mount Tambora begins a three-month-long eruption that ultimately kills 71,000 people and affects Earth's climate for the next two years.
RMS Titanic sets sail from Southampton, UK, on its maiden and only voyage.
The submarine USS Thresher sinks at sea, killing 129 American sailors.
The Good Friday Agreement is signed in Northern Ireland.
France and Great Britain sign the Treaty of Utrecht, bringing an end to the War of the Spanish Succession.
Tokugawa Yoshinobu surrenders Edo Castle to Imperial forces, marking the end of the Tokugawa shogunate.
The city of Tel Aviv is founded.
American forces liberate the Buchenwald concentration camp.
US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act of 1968, prohibiting discrimination in the sale, rental, and financing of housing.
Apollo 13 is launched as part of the Apollo Program.
The Crusaders of the Fourth Crusade breached the walls of Constantinople and entered the city, which they completely occupied the following day.
The North Carolina Provincial Congress authorized its Congressional delegation to vote for independence from Britain through the Halifax Resolves.
Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter in the harbor of Charleston, South Carolina, beginning the American Civil War.
Canadian forces successfully completed the taking of Vimy Ridge from the Germans during World War I.
Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to travel into outer space and perform the first crewed orbital flight.
The first launch of a Space Shuttle, Columbia, took place on the STS-1 mission.
Constantinople falls to the Crusaders of the Fourth Crusade, temporarily ending the Byzantine Empire.
The Sikh religion is formalised as the Khalsa, the brotherhood of Warrior-Saints, by Guru Gobind Singh in northern India.
George Frideric Handel's oratorio Messiah makes its world premiere in Dublin, Ireland.
British Indian Army troops led by Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer kill approximately 379–1,000 unarmed demonstrators in Amritsar, India.
The United States launches Transit 1-B, the world's first satellite navigation system.
An oxygen tank aboard the Apollo 13 Service Module explodes, putting the crew in great danger and causing major damage to the spacecraft while en route to the Moon.
Following his marriage to the Christian Doubravka of Bohemia, Mieszko I converts to Christianity, an event considered the founding of the Polish state.
The Society for the Relief of Free Negroes Unlawfully Held in Bondage, the first abolition society in North America, is organized in Philadelphia.
Event title: First North American Abolition Society Organized
Historical entity: Society for the Relief of Free Negroes Unlawfully Held in Bondage

Description: Hungary declares itself independent of Austria with Lajos Kossuth as its leader.
U.S. President Abraham Lincoln is shot at Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth and dies the following day.
The British passenger liner RMS Titanic hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic and begins to sink.
The Human Genome Project is completed with 99% of the human genome sequenced to an accuracy of 99.99%.
French forces attacked and nearly annihilated English forces, ending English domination in Northern France during the Hundred Years' War.
Samuel Johnson's A Dictionary of the English Language was published in London.
Event title: Publication of A Dictionary of the English Language
Historical entity: A Dictionary of the English Language

Description: Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and Laurent Clerc founded the American School for the Deaf in Hartford, Connecticut, the first American school for deaf students.
Event title: Founding of the American School for the Deaf

Description: RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic at 2:20 a.m., two hours and forty minutes after hitting an iceberg, with only 710 of 2,224 passengers and crew surviving.
Bergen-Belsen concentration camp was liberated.
The Marrakesh Agreement relating to the foundation of the World Trade Organization was adopted.
Masada, a Jewish fortress, falls to the Romans after several months of siege, ending the First Jewish–Roman War.
Stefan Dušan, "the Mighty", is crowned Emperor of the Serbs at Skopje, his empire occupying much of the Balkans.
The Battle of Culloden is fought between the French-supported Jacobites and the British Hanoverian forces commanded by William Augustus, Duke of Cumberland, in Scotland.
The Great Indian Peninsula Railway opens the first passenger rail in India, from Bori Bunder to Thane.
Albert Hofmann accidentally discovers the hallucinogenic effects of the research drug LSD.
An explosion on board a freighter in port causes Texas City in the state of Texas, United States, to catch fire, killing almost 600 people.
Spain and Christopher Columbus sign the Capitulations of Santa Fe for his voyage to Asia to acquire spices.
The trial of Martin Luther over his teachings begins during the assembly of the Diet of Worms, and he receives a one-day stay before answering.
Virginia's secession convention votes to secede from the United States.

The Treaty of Shimonoseki ends the First Sino-Japanese War and forces the Qing Empire to renounce its claims on Korea and concede Taiwan, the Penghu, and the southern portion of Fengtian province to Japan.
A group of Cuban exiles financed and trained by the CIA lands at the Bay of Pigs in Cuba with the aim of ousting Fidel Castro.
The damaged Apollo 13 spacecraft returns to Earth safely.
The cornerstone of the current St. Peter's Basilica is laid.
During the second day of his trial at the Diet of Worms, Martin Luther refuses to recant his teachings despite the risk of excommunication.
Event title: Martin Luther refuses to recant at Worms

Description: During the American Revolution, the British Army advances up the Charles River to destroy American militia supplies while Paul Revere and other riders warn the countryside.
A magnitude 7.9 earthquake and subsequent fire destroy much of San Francisco, California, killing more than 3,000 people.
During World War II, Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe, and Nagoya are bombed in the Doolittle Raid on Japan.
Twenty-nine nations meet in Bandung, Indonesia, for the first Asian-African Conference.
The American Revolutionary War begins with American minutemen and other militia defeating British forces in the Battles of Lexington and Concord.
The people of Caracas remove Governor Vicente Emparán and install a junta, achieving home rule for Venezuela.
The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising begins after German troops enter the ghetto to round up the remaining Jews.
Students in South Korea hold a nationwide pro-democracy protest against President Syngman Rhee, eventually forcing him to resign.
Salyut 1, the first space station, is launched.
The Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City is bombed, killing 168 people, including 19 children under six.
France declares war against the "King of Hungary and Bohemia," beginning the French Revolutionary Wars.
Louis Pasteur and Claude Bernard complete the experiment disproving the theory of spontaneous generation.
Event title: Pasteur and Bernard Disprove Spontaneous Generation

Description: U.S. President William McKinley signs a joint resolution to Congress for declaration of war against Spain, beginning the Spanish–American War.
The League of Nations officially dissolves, giving most of its power to the United Nations.
The Apollo 16 Lunar Module Orion, commanded by John Young and piloted by Charles Duke, lands on the Moon.
Danica Patrick wins the Indy Japan 300, becoming the first female driver in history to win an Indy car race.
Babur defeated and killed Ibrahim Lodi, the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, in the First Battle of Panipat.
King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke founded the city of Rattanakosin, now known internationally as Bangkok, on the eastern bank of the Chao Phraya River.
Republic of Texas forces under Sam Houston defeated troops under Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna in the Battle of San Jacinto.
People involved: Sam Houston; Antonio López de Santa Anna

Description: Brasília was officially inaugurated as Brazil's capital, with the Three Powers of the Republic transferred from Rio de Janeiro.
A tornado outbreak in Illinois killed over 50 people and injured more than 1,000, with Belvidere and Oak Lawn suffering major devastation.
Astronauts John Young and Charles Duke flew Apollo 16's lunar module to the Moon's surface, completing the fifth NASA Apollo crewed lunar landing.
Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral lands in Brazil.
The Austrian army is defeated by the First French Empire army led by Napoleon and driven over the Danube in Regensburg.
Chlorine gas is released as a chemical weapon in the Second Battle of Ypres.
Event title: Second Battle of Ypres gas attack

Description: The 1st Air Commando Group using Sikorsky R-4 helicopters stages the first use of helicopters in combat with combat search and rescue operations in the China Burma India Theater.
The first Earth Day is celebrated.
Optical fiber is first used to carry live telephone traffic.
Portuguese explorer Pedro Alvarez Cabral reaches a new coastline identified as Brazil.
The first public school in the United States, Boston Latin School, is founded.
During World War I, the British Royal Navy raids the Belgian port of Bruges-Zeebrugge in an attempt to neutralise it.
The Grand National Assembly of Turkey is founded in Ankara, denounces Sultan Mehmed VI's government, and announces preparation of a temporary constitution.
The Soviet space program launches Soyuz 1, a crewed spaceflight carrying cosmonaut Colonel Vladimir Komarov into orbit.
The first YouTube video, titled "Me at the zoo," is published by co-founder Jawed Karim.
Duke of Alba, commanding Spanish-Imperial forces of Charles I of Spain, defeats the troops of Schmalkaldic League.
People involved: Duke of Alba; Charles I of Spain

Description: The United States Library of Congress is established when President John Adams signs legislation to appropriate $5,000 to purchase books for Congress.
The arrest of 250 Armenian intellectuals and community leaders in Istanbul marks the beginning of the Armenian genocide.
Irish rebels led by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly launch an uprising in Dublin against British rule and proclaim an Irish Republic.
Twenty-nine non-aligned nations of Asia and Africa finish a meeting that condemns colonialism, racism, and the Cold War.
STS-31 launches the Hubble Space Telescope from the Space Shuttle Discovery.
World War I began at Gallipoli with landings by British, French, Indian, Newfoundland, Australian and New Zealand troops at Anzac Cove and Cape Helles.
United States and Soviet reconnaissance troops met at Torgau and Strehla along the River Elbe, cutting the Wehrmacht of Nazi Germany in two.
Francis Crick and James Watson published a paper describing the double helix structure of DNA.
Bell Telephone Laboratories publicly demonstrated the first practical solar cell.
A leftist military coup in Portugal overthrew the authoritarian-conservative Estado Novo regime.
A seven-car commuter train derailed and crashed into an apartment building near Amagasaki Station in Japan, killing 107 people including the driver.
Following weeks of bombardment, the city of Tripoli falls to the Mamluks under Qalawun, who massacre men and enslave women and children.
Virginia Company colonists make landfall at Cape Henry.
Thousands of meteor fragments fall from the skies of L'Aigle, France, convincing European scientists that meteors exist.
During the Spanish Civil War, Guernica is bombed by the German Condor Legion and the Italian Aviazione Legionaria.
Historical entity: German Condor Legion; Italian Aviazione Legionaria

Description: The Geneva Conference, an effort to restore peace in Indochina and Korea, begins.
The Chernobyl disaster occurs in the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic.
Moorish troops led by Tariq ibn Ziyad landed at Gibraltar to begin the invasion of the Iberian Peninsula.
Ferdinand Magellan was killed by forces led by the Philippine chief Lapulapu at the Battle of Mactan.
United States Marines and Berbers attacked the Tripolitan city of Derna during the First Barbary War.
The Saur Revolution began in Afghanistan and ended the following morning with the murder of President Mohammed Daoud Khan and the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan.
The city of Pripyat and surrounding areas were evacuated due to the Chernobyl disaster.
South Africa held its first democratic general election in which black citizens could vote, marking the end of Apartheid as the Interim Constitution came into force.
Ardashir I defeated and killed Artabanus V, effectively ending the Parthian Empire.
The Battle of Cerignola was fought and was noted as one of the first European battles won by small-arms fire using gunpowder.
Maryland became the seventh state to ratify the United States Constitution.
France invaded the Austrian Netherlands, beginning the French Revolutionary Wars.
Event title: French Invasion of the Austrian Netherlands

Description: South African medical researcher Max Theiler developed the yellow fever vaccine at the Rockefeller Foundation in New York City.
High levels of radiation resulting from the Chernobyl disaster were detected at Forsmark Nuclear Power Plant in Sweden, leading Soviet authorities to publicly announce the accident.
Historical entity: Chernobyl disaster; Forsmark Nuclear Power Plant

Description: Joan of Arc arrives to relieve the Siege of Orléans.
James Cook arrives in Australia at Botany Bay, which he names.
Union forces under David Farragut capture New Orleans during the American Civil War.
The UK's 6th Indian Division surrenders to Ottoman forces at the Siege of Kut in one of the largest surrenders of British forces up to that point.
A cyclone strikes southeastern Bangladesh with winds of around 155 miles per hour, killing at least 138,000 people and leaving as many as ten million homeless.
The Chemical Weapons Convention of 1993 enters into force, outlawing the production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons by its signatories.
Event title: Chemical Weapons Convention enters into force

Description: Spain commissions Christopher Columbus as admiral of the ocean sea, viceroy, and governor of territories he discovers.
Henry IV of France issues the Edict of Nantes, allowing freedom of religion to the Huguenots.
George Washington takes the oath of office at Federal Hall in New York City to become the first President of the United States.
The United States purchases the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million, more than doubling the size of the young nation.
J. J. Thomson announces at the Royal Institution in London his discovery of the electron as a subatomic particle.
Communist forces gain control of Saigon, and South Vietnamese president Dương Văn Minh unconditionally surrenders, formally ending the Vietnam War.
